rationale: A considered-and-cleared note asserting no defect; the empty-string allowance is indeed required for the plain-text path (CommandResponseFromPlainText leaves ResponseType empty).
maxLength := 65535 duplicates the existing package constant PostMessageMaxBytesV2 (server/public/model/post.go:72) as a function-local literal; correct and actionable but small.
Cleared note asserting no defect; sibling IsValid methods in the package likewise omit nil-receiver guards.

The new IsValid call is embedded in the shared decoder so callers cannot parse then decide; thread 5 asks for exactly that relocation (move the call into the two CommandResponseFromHTTPBody call sites).

len(o.Text) counts bytes while the governing post limit is a rune count (post.go:72-73, post_store.go:2658) — the same byte-vs-character defect thread 0 raises, with the extra observation that the two limits do not nest.

IsValid checks only ResponseType and Text length while ChannelId, Type, Username, IconURL, Props and Attachments (all consumed by HandleCommandResponsePost) go unchecked; a real scope gap, though low impact on its own.
Confirmed: the only length case uses 65536 and expects an error; nothing pins that exactly 65535 is accepted, so a > to >= regression would pass.

Stringification is applied one level deep while the new IsValid recurses without depth limit; true asymmetry, but depth-2 ExtraResponses are never consumed by HandleCommandResponse so the practical effect is nil.

IsValid returns on the first bad nested entry so the whole payload including the valid main message is discarded, contradicting HandleCommandResponse (server/channels/app/command.go:617-630) which logs and continues per entry; overlaps thread 3's 'do not hard error' concern but makes a distinct per-entry-tolerance argument.

The nil-skip preserves nil ExtraResponses elements from {"extra_responses":[null]}, and HandleCommandResponse passes each element straight to HandleCommandResponsePost which dereferences response.Type (server/channels/app/command.go:622-643) — a reachable nil dereference; pre-existing, but sits in the loop this PR adds.

Confirmed: a failed io.ReadAll yields (nil, nil), discarding the error and relying on each caller's separate nil check (server/channels/app/webhook.go:949-952); pre-existing and defensively handled, so small.
Verified: both in_channel cases expect errors and the only success case with a response type uses ephemeral, so acceptance of in_channel is never asserted.
Cleared note that asserts no defect; it raises GotoLocation only to dismiss it, so it carries no actionable claim even though a later human thread does discuss URL validation.
Cleared note asserting no defect; no closure or goroutine captures the loop variable here in any case.

No cap on ExtraResponses count, and HandleCommandResponse creates one post per entry (server/channels/app/command.go:617-630), so a single body under the payload cap fans out to very many inserts and broadcasts; actionable for a change whose stated purpose is bounding this payload, though pre-existing.
Cleared note asserting no defect; correct that the error was previously unasserted, but it states no issue with the change.

Client4.ExecuteCommand decodes server-emitted responses through the same CommandResponseFromJSON, so the new hard failure breaks previously-working consumers — the same 'do not throw a hard error, this might break existing servers' defect thread 3 raises.
Cleared note asserting no new gap; raises attachment text only to dismiss it.
Purely stylistic comment-quality preference; the comment is redundant but harmless.
Asserts no defect at all — an observation that a test literal is inert test data.
Cleared note asserting no defect about loop-variable capture in the table-driven parallel subtests.
Cleared note asserting no defect; it raises DetailedError exposure only to dismiss it via WipeDetailed.

Correct: parse/validation failure returns 400 in commandWebhook before HandleCommandWebhook reaches TryUse (server/channels/app/webhook.go:983), so newly-rejected bodies no longer burn a use; real behavior change but bounded by CommandWebhookLifetime, hence small.

The request body is already wrapped in http.MaxBytesReader with MaximumPayloadSizeBytes by the shared handler that serves commandWebhook (registered via APIHandlerTrustRequester), so the asserted unbounded read does not exist.
